answer: PoA identity verification binds each claimed agent to a VDF transcript produced by continuous sequential modular squarings. Since each squaring depends on the prior result, an attacker simulating many clones cannot distribute one chain across GPUs to reduce its latency; each clone therefore incurs a strict physical time bottleneck. Wesolowski proofs make outputs efficiently verifiable, while plume, pigment, and cedar are protocol labels rather than computational shortcuts.
